content.user_title: Review Code for Security and Quality
content.value_statement: Code reviews can miss security, quality, performance, and test risks. This skill provides a structured workflow, checklists, and helper script for consistent review.
actual_capabilities: Guides security review for injection, authentication, secrets, XSS, deserialization, and cryptography issues.
Provides a broad code review checklist for security, quality, performance, tests, documentation, and deployment readiness.
Includes a helper script for Bandit, Radon, Pylint, Safety, and report generation.
Supplies performance review guidance for algorithms, database queries, memory, network calls, caching, and concurrency.
Offers language-specific review prompts for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Go.
limitations: The helper script depends on external tools that must be installed separately.
Automated scanner output still requires human review and project context.
The references are general and may need adaptation for specific frameworks or policies.
The skill does not replace secure design review or production penetration testing.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Use the workflow and checklist to inspect a proposed change before merge.

use_cases.title: Run a Security-Focused Audit
use_cases.description: Use the security patterns and helper script to find common vulnerability classes.

use_cases.title: Define Team Review Standards
use_cases.description: Adapt the checklist and feedback patterns into a repeatable review process.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small change
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this change for correctness, readability, tests, and obvious security risks. Prioritize findings by severity and cite the affected files.

prompt_templates.title: Security Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this code for injection, access control, secrets handling, unsafe deserialization, XSS, and weak cryptography. Report only evidence-backed issues.

prompt_templates.title: Performance Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Optimization pass for a service or feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this implementation for algorithmic cost, database query efficiency, memory use, network timeouts, caching, and concurrency risks.

prompt_templates.title: Release Gate Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release readiness review across security, correctness, reliability, performance, tests, documentation, migration risk, and operational rollback needs.

output_examples.input: A pull request adds a new login endpoint and updates session handling.
output: High: Missing rate limiting on repeated login attempts.
Medium: Session timeout behavior is not covered by tests.
Low: Error messages can be clearer without exposing sensitive details.

output_examples.input: A service endpoint now fetches data from several remote APIs.
output: High: Remote requests need explicit connect and read timeouts.
Medium: Sequential calls may add avoidable latency under load.
Suggested: Add retry limits and structured failure logging.

output_examples.input: A team wants a reusable checklist for merge reviews.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a structured checklist covering security, quality, performance, tests, documentation, deployment, and follow-up actions.

best_practices: Run automated checks first, then use human review for logic, design, and risk tradeoffs.
Ask for file and line references so every finding is easy to verify.
Separate blocking defects from suggestions so authors can act quickly.
anti_patterns: Do not treat scanner output as final without reviewing context and exploitability.
Do not mix style preferences with security or correctness findings.
Do not review large unrelated changes without first defining the scope.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews security, quality, performance, tests, documentation, and release readiness for code changes.

faq.question: Does it run tools automatically?
faq.answer: It includes a helper script, but the user must run it in an environment with the required tools installed.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance emphasizes Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Java, and Go, with general principles for other languages.

faq.question: Can it replace a human reviewer?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure review and find common issues, but human judgment remains necessary.

faq.question: Is this useful for security teams?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes vulnerability patterns, secure alternatives, and prompts for focused security review.

faq.question: Can teams customize it?
faq.answer: Yes. Teams can adjust thresholds, checklist items, and review prompts for their standards.
